ideas.title: Add React Query hooks for Tenant Service
ideas.description: Create React Query hooks for tenant management (getCurrent, getSubscription, getLicense, getStats, upgradePlan, cancelSubscription, getBillingPortalUrl). This enables tenant admin dashboards to use the same hooks pattern as other SDK services.
ideas.rationale: tenant.service.ts exists with 7 complete methods but has no corresponding React Query hooks. The hook pattern is mature in use-discount-codes.ts and use-organizations.ts. Query key factory pattern in query-keys.ts can be extended.
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add tenant key factory to query-keys.ts (tenant: { all, current, subscription, license, stats }). 2. Create use-tenant.ts with hooks: useTenant(), useTenantSubscription(), useTenantLicense(), useTenantStats(), useUpgradePlan(), useCancelSubscription(), useBillingPortalUrl(). 3. Export from hooks/index.ts. Follow the existing hook pattern with staleTime for read operations.

ideas.title: Add React Query hooks for User Group Service
ideas.description: Create React Query hooks for user group management (getUserGroup, list user groups, create user group). Enables backoffice admin UIs to manage pricing user groups (U19, ADULT_ORG, OTHER) using the standard hooks pattern.
ideas.rationale: user-group.service.ts exports userGroupService and backofficeUserGroupsService with 4 methods total but no React Query hooks exist. Pattern is well-established in other CRUD services like use-seasons.ts and use-discount-codes.ts.
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add userGroups key factory to query-keys.ts (userGroups: { all, lists, list, my }). 2. Create use-user-groups.ts with hooks: useUserGroups(), useMyUserGroup(), useCreateUserGroup(). 3. Include staleTime of 5 minutes (rarely changes). 4. Export from hooks/index.ts.

ideas.title: Add React Query hooks for Price Rules Service
ideas.description: Create React Query hooks for backoffice price rules management (getPriceRules, replacePriceRules, getListingRules, upsertListingRules). Enables admin UIs to manage listing-specific pricing without direct service calls.
ideas.rationale: price-rules.service.ts exports BackofficePriceRulesService with 4 methods but no hooks. The hooks pattern for backoffice admin CRUD is established in use-seasons.ts and use-rental-objects.ts.
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add priceRules key factory to query-keys.ts with listing scoping. 2. Create use-price-rules.ts with hooks: usePriceRules(listingId), useReplacePriceRules(), useListingRules(listingId), useUpsertListingRules(). 3. Mutations should invalidate both priceRules and rentalObjects keys. 4. Export from hooks/index.ts.

ideas.title: Add User Settings and Booking Policy hooks
ideas.description: Extend settings hooks to cover user settings, booking policy, and branding. Currently only useTenantSettings and useUpdateTenantSettings exist in use-integrations.ts, but settings.service.ts has 9 methods including getUserSettings, updateUserSettings, getBookingPolicy, updateBookingPolicy, getBranding, updateBranding.
ideas.rationale: settings.service.ts has comprehensive methods for user preferences and booking configuration, but only tenant settings have hooks. The hook pattern from use-integrations.ts can be extended to cover all settings endpoints.
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Create dedicated use-settings.ts hook file. 2. Add hooks: useUserSettings(), useUpdateUserSettings(), useBookingPolicy(), useUpdateBookingPolicy(), useBranding(), useUpdateBranding(), useResetSettings(). 3. Extend query-keys.ts settings section with user/booking/branding keys. 4. Add optimistic updates to mutation hooks. 5. Export from hooks/index.ts.

ideas.title: Add Share Service and SDK hooks for shareable links
ideas.description: Create SDK service and React Query hooks for the share API (createShareLink, getShareData). The API exists at /api/share but has no SDK coverage. Enables listing and booking sharing functionality through the SDK-first architecture.
ideas.rationale: apps/api/src/modules/share/share.controller.ts exists with create and get endpoints but no corresponding SDK service or hooks. The service pattern from booking.service.ts and hooks pattern from use-discount-codes.ts can be replicated.
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Create share.service.ts with ShareService class extending BaseService. Methods: createShareLink(type, resourceId, expiresIn), getShareData(token). 2. Export from services/index.ts. 3. Add share key factory to query-keys.ts. 4. Create use-share.ts with hooks: useShareData(token), useCreateShareLink() with mutation. 5. Export from hooks/index.ts. Types: ShareData, CreateShareLinkDTO.

ideas.title: Localize @xala/ds ConfirmDialog and AlertDialog default button text
ideas.description: The ConfirmDialog and AlertDialog components in @xala/ds have hardcoded Norwegian default strings ('Bekreft', 'Avbryt', 'Lukk', 'Vennligst vent...') which breaks the multi-language experience for English users
ideas.rationale: The CLAUDE.md mandates i18n-first development with useT() hooks. Design system components should accept localized strings or provide i18n integration to support both Norwegian and English users. Currently users see mixed-language UI when using dialogs from the design system.
ideas.current_state: Line 212-213: confirmText='Bekreft' (Norwegian 'Confirm'), cancelText='Avbryt' (Norwegian 'Cancel'). Line 295: Loading state shows hardcoded 'Vennligst vent...' (Norwegian 'Please wait...'). Line 325: closeText='Lukk' (Norwegian 'Close').
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Remove default values from button text props, making them required. This forces consuming apps to explicitly pass localized strings via t('common.confirm'), t('common.cancel'), etc. 2. Alternatively, add an optional i18n prop that accepts a translation function. 3. Update the JSDoc examples to show proper i18n usage pattern. Example: <ConfirmDialog confirmText={t('common.confirm')} cancelText={t('common.cancel')} loadingText={t('common.pleaseWait')} />
ideas.user_benefit: English-speaking municipal staff will see consistent language in confirmation dialogs instead of mixed Norwegian/English UI when interacting with critical actions like delete or cancel

ideas.title: Add i18n support to Backoffice sidebar navigation labels
ideas.description: The backoffice Sidebar.tsx component has all navigation labels and descriptions hardcoded in Norwegian ('Dashboard', 'Oversikt og statistikk', 'Administrasjon', etc.) instead of using the @xala/i18n translation system
ideas.rationale: Unlike minside Sidebar which properly uses useT() for translations, the backoffice sidebar bypasses i18n completely. This violates CLAUDE.md rule: 'NEVER use hardcoded strings in UI components'. Municipal staff who prefer English cannot use the backoffice in their language.
ideas.current_state: Lines 164-234 contain 50+ hardcoded Norwegian strings: 'Dashboard' (167), 'Oversikt og statistikk' (167), 'Listings' (173), 'Administrer utleieobjekter' (173), 'Kalender' (174), 'Visuell oversikt' (174). Section titles 'Administrasjon' (172), 'Kommunikasjon' (181), 'Brukere & Org' (186), etc. are all hardcoded.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Add import: import { useT } from '@xala/i18n'; 2. Add const t = useT(); in Sidebar function. 3. Replace each hardcoded string: name: t('backoffice.nav.dashboard'), description: t('backoffice.nav.dashboardDesc'). 4. Add 100+ new i18n keys to packages/i18n/src/locales/nb.ts and en.ts under backoffice.nav.* namespace.
ideas.user_benefit: Backoffice admin users can switch to English language and see fully translated navigation, improving accessibility for non-Norwegian speaking municipal staff and consultants

ideas.title: Fix LoadingFallback Spinner size attribute typo (data-data-size)
ideas.description: LoadingFallback.tsx has a typo where 'data-data-size' should be 'data-size', causing the Spinner to render at default size instead of large size during page transitions
ideas.rationale: This is a bug that affects perceived loading performance. When users navigate between routes with lazy loading, they see a small spinner instead of a prominent large spinner. The small spinner can be hard to notice against the full-screen background, making the app feel unresponsive.
ideas.current_state: Line 18: <Spinner aria-label="Laster..." data-data-size="lg" /> - The attribute 'data-data-size' is incorrect (duplicated 'data-' prefix). Additionally, aria-label uses hardcoded Norwegian 'Laster...' instead of i18n.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Change 'data-data-size="lg"' to 'data-size="lg"' on line 18. 2. Add import { useT } from '@xala/i18n'; 3. Convert to function component to use hooks, or pass aria-label as prop from parent. 4. Change aria-label from hardcoded 'Laster...' to t('common.loading'). Simple one-line fix for the typo, i18n fix requires function component conversion.
ideas.user_benefit: Users will see a properly sized loading spinner during route transitions, providing clearer visual feedback that content is loading. Non-Norwegian users will hear correct screen reader text.

ideas.title: Localize NotificationCenter component all user-facing strings
ideas.description: The NotificationCenter component in @xala/ds has 15+ hardcoded Norwegian strings for filter tabs, empty states, headings, buttons, and ARIA labels that need i18n support
ideas.rationale: Notification center is a high-frequency user interaction point. Having mixed language breaks the user experience for English-speaking users. All text appears in Norwegian regardless of user's language preference.
ideas.current_state: Lines 98-100: Filter tab labels 'Alle', 'Uleste', 'Leste'. Lines 176-189: Empty state messages in Norwegian (3 variations). Line 323: 'Varsler' heading. Line 338: 'Merk alle som lest' button. Line 344: aria-label='Lukk varselssenter'. Line 391: Spinner aria-label='Laster varsler...'
ideas.proposed_change: Add localization props interface: interface NotificationCenterLabels { title: string; filterAll: string; filterUnread: string; filterRead: string; markAllAsRead: string; closeAriaLabel: string; loadingAriaLabel: string; emptyAll: { title: string; description: string }; emptyUnread: { title: string; description: string }; emptyRead: { title: string; description: string }; }. Make labels prop required so consuming apps pass t() values.
ideas.user_benefit: Users viewing the notification center will see consistent language throughout, improving comprehension and accessibility for English-speaking municipal staff

ideas.title: Add visible focus indicator to Drawer close button for keyboard navigation
ideas.description: The Drawer component's close button has hover styles but no visible focus indicator for keyboard users, making it difficult to navigate the drawer using keyboard-only navigation (WCAG 2.4.7 violation)
ideas.rationale: WCAG 2.1 AA requires visible focus indicators (Success Criterion 2.4.7). The close button uses onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave for hover states but has no :focus-visible styling. Keyboard users cannot see when the close button is focused, creating accessibility barrier for users who can't use a mouse.
ideas.current_state: Lines 439-466: Close button has hover states via onMouseEnter (backgroundColor change, color change) and onMouseLeave (reset) but no onFocus/onBlur handlers. The button also has hardcoded aria-label='Lukk' (Norwegian for 'Close') on line 442.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Add onFocus handler: onFocus={(e) => { e.currentTarget.style.outline = '2px solid var(--ds-color-focus-outer)'; e.currentTarget.style.outlineOffset = '2px'; e.currentTarget.style.backgroundColor = 'var(--ds-color-neutral-surface-hover)'; }}. 2. Add onBlur handler to reset styles. 3. Add closeAriaLabel prop to DrawerProps interface for localization. 4. Change default from 'Lukk' to 'Close' (English default for design system components).
ideas.user_benefit: Keyboard users will be able to clearly see when the close button is focused while tabbing through the drawer, and screen reader users will hear localized labels appropriate to their language setting

ideas.title: Restrict CORS to trusted origins only
ideas.description: The Fastify adapter configures CORS with `origin: '*'` and `allowedHeaders: '*'`, allowing any domain to make cross-origin requests to the API. This is a critical misconfiguration for a multi-tenant municipal system handling sensitive citizen data including Norwegian national IDs (NIN), booking information, and GDPR-protected data.
ideas.rationale: Wildcard CORS allows malicious websites to make authenticated requests on behalf of logged-in users, potentially leading to data theft or unauthorized actions. In a government/municipal context handling PII, this violates GDPR requirements and Norwegian data protection regulations. The CORS_ORIGINS environment variable is already defined with production URLs but is not being used.
ideas.currentRisk: Any malicious website can make authenticated API requests when a user is logged in, stealing PII or performing unauthorized bookings
ideas.remediation: Replace wildcard CORS with an allowlist of trusted frontend domains. Use the existing `CORS_ORIGINS` environment variable: `origin: process.env.CORS_ORIGINS?.split(',') || ['http://localhost:5173', 'http://localhost:5174', 'http://localhost:5175']`. Also restrict `allowedHeaders` to specific required headers like 'Content-Type', 'Authorization', 'x-tenant-id', 'x-user-id'.

ideas.title: Replace predictable CSRF token generation with cryptographically secure tokens
ideas.description: The AuthController.getCsrf() method in auth.controller.ts generates CSRF tokens using `Buffer.from(Date.now().toString()).toString('base64')`, which produces completely predictable tokens that can be easily guessed by attackers. The token is just a base64-encoded timestamp with no cryptographic randomness.
ideas.rationale: CSRF tokens must be unpredictable to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks. A token derived from the current timestamp can be calculated by any attacker who knows the approximate request time (within seconds), completely defeating CSRF protection for state-changing operations like bookings and consent management.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
ideas.currentRisk: Attackers can predict CSRF tokens and forge requests that appear to come from legitimate users, enabling unauthorized bookings or data modifications
ideas.remediation: Use Node.js crypto module to generate cryptographically secure random tokens: `import crypto from 'crypto'; const csrfToken = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex');`. Consider using @fastify/csrf-protection plugin for production-grade CSRF handling with token binding to sessions.

ideas.title: Implement password verification in email/password login endpoint
ideas.description: The login endpoint at POST /api/auth/login in auth.controller.ts finds users by email but does not verify passwords. Lines 29-42 query the user by email, and if found, immediately generate a JWT token without any password validation. The function claims to be 'Email/password login' but only checks the email exists.
ideas.rationale: Email addresses are often publicly known or easily guessable, especially for municipality staff (firstname.lastname@kommune.no pattern). Without password verification, the entire authentication system is bypassed, giving attackers full access to any user account including admin roles.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
ideas.currentRisk: Anyone can log in as any user (including admin accounts) by simply knowing or guessing their email address. No credential validation occurs.
ideas.remediation: 1) Add password_hash column to users table using bcrypt/argon2. 2) Require password in login request body with Zod validation. 3) Compare hashed passwords before issuing JWT: `const isValid = await bcrypt.compare(body.password, user.passwordHash); if (!isValid) return 401;`. 4) Return generic 'Invalid credentials' error for both wrong email and wrong password to prevent user enumeration.

ideas.title: Disable GraphiQL playground in production environment
ideas.description: The API registers the GraphQL endpoint in main.ts with `graphiql: true`, enabling the interactive GraphQL playground in all environments including production. This exposes the complete API schema, allows arbitrary query execution, and provides introspection capabilities to potential attackers.
ideas.rationale: GraphiQL in production exposes internal API structure for reconnaissance. Attackers can discover undocumented queries, understand data relationships, and craft complex nested queries that could cause denial of service. For a government platform handling sensitive municipal data, API introspection should be disabled in production.
ideas.currentRisk: Attackers can explore the full GraphQL schema, discover all available queries/mutations, understand data models, and potentially craft expensive nested queries to overload the server
ideas.remediation: Conditionally enable GraphiQL only in development: `graphiql: process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'`. Also add query complexity limits and depth limiting using mercurius validation: `validationRules: [depthLimit(10), queryComplexity({ maximumComplexity: 1000 })]`.

ideas.title: Remove sensitive PII from ID-porten authentication debug logging
ideas.description: The ID-porten authentication controller (idporten.controller.ts) contains 40+ console.log statements that output highly sensitive data including Norwegian National Identity Numbers (NIN/fødselsnummer), full session data objects, cookie contents, JWT tokens, and user details. These are production console statements, not conditionally disabled.
ideas.rationale: Norwegian NIN is among the most sensitive PII under GDPR and Norwegian personal data regulations. The logs include statements like `console.log('Full session data:', JSON.stringify(sessionData))` and `console.log('Extracted NIN:', nin)`. This data in logs creates compliance violations, breach liability, and potential vectors for identity theft.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
ideas.currentRisk: Norwegian national IDs, session tokens, and authentication data are written to production logs, violating GDPR Article 32 (security of processing) and creating significant breach liability under Norwegian data protection law
ideas.remediation: 1) Replace all console.log with the existing pino logger that has field redaction configured for 'ssn', 'cookie', 'token'. 2) Remove NIN logging entirely or mask to first 6 digits pattern. 3) Wrap debug-level logs in environment check: `if (process.env.LOG_LEVEL === 'debug')`. 4) Never log full session objects - extract only safe identifiers for tracing.

ideas.title: Create CONTRIBUTING.md with contribution guidelines
ideas.description: The monorepo lacks a CONTRIBUTING.md file at the root level. Currently, new developers have no formal onboarding guide for contributing code, running tests, or understanding the PR workflow. There's no guidance on commit message conventions, branch naming, or code review processes.
ideas.rationale: A CONTRIBUTING.md is essential for open-source best practices and team onboarding. It establishes clear expectations for code contributions, reduces friction for new developers, and ensures consistent code quality across the team. Most professional projects have this as a standard file.
ideas.currentDocumentation: No CONTRIBUTING.md exists at root level
ideas.proposedContent: Create comprehensive CONTRIBUTING.md covering: 1) Development setup, 2) Code style/linting rules, 3) Branch naming conventions, 4) Commit message format (Co-Authored-By pattern), 5) PR process and review checklist, 6) Testing requirements, 7) Design system compliance requirements, 8) SDK-first rule adherence, 9) i18n localization requirements

ideas.title: Add README.md documentation to @xala/i18n package
ideas.description: The packages/i18n directory is missing a README.md file. The i18n package provides critical localization functionality (useT hook, nb/en translations) but has no package-level documentation explaining its API, usage patterns, or how to add new translations. Developers must read source code to understand usage.
ideas.rationale: The i18n package is used across all three frontend apps (web, backoffice, minside) and is referenced extensively in CLAUDE.md rules. Without README documentation, developers struggle to understand: how to add new translation keys, the key naming conventions (common.*, auth.*, nav.*), how to use the useT() hook, and how the locale switching works.
ideas.currentDocumentation: Only docs/packages/06-i18n.md exists but no package-level README; docs/I18N_SCAN_REPORT references i18n but doesn't document API
ideas.proposedContent: Create README with: 1) Quick start examples, 2) useT() hook usage with TypeScript, 3) Translation key naming conventions (common.*, auth.*, nav.*, bookings.*, etc.), 4) How to add new translations to both nb.ts and en.ts, 5) Locale switching API, 6) Integration examples for React components, 7) i18n scanner usage

ideas.title: Create comprehensive environment variables reference
ideas.description: Environment variables are scattered across multiple .env.example files in apps/web, apps/backoffice, apps/minside, and apps/api without centralized documentation. Each app has 6-15 required environment variables but there's no single reference explaining what each variable does, valid values, and security considerations.
ideas.rationale: New developers and DevOps personnel waste time figuring out which environment variables are required. Sensitive variables like VITE_MAPBOX_TOKEN, JWT_SECRET, IDPORTEN_CLIENT_SECRET need clear documentation on how to obtain and secure them. This is critical for deployment and local development setup. The project_index.json shows 40+ environment variables across apps.
ideas.currentDocumentation: Only .env.example files exist with minimal comments; docs/guides/03-deployment.md touches on environment but not comprehensive
ideas.proposedContent: Create reference doc covering: 1) All VITE_* frontend variables by app, 2) API server variables (DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, SESSION_SECRET, etc.), 3) Third-party service tokens (Mapbox, Sentry, ID-porten), 4) Multi-tenant configuration (VITE_TENANT_ID), 5) Security best practices for secrets, 6) Local development defaults vs production, 7) WebSocket URL configuration (VITE_WS_URL)

ideas.title: Document API error codes and handling patterns
ideas.description: While the codebase mentions RFC 7807 Problem Details for errors, there's no comprehensive reference of all error codes, their meanings, and recommended handling patterns. The SDK throws ApiError with codes like VALIDATION_ERROR, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, INTERNAL_ERROR but no exhaustive list exists with all business-specific error types.
ideas.rationale: Frontend developers need to know all possible error codes to implement proper error handling UI. The SDK README shows basic error handling but doesn't list all error types specific to booking conflicts, rate limiting, GDPR violations, or tenant isolation errors. This leads to inconsistent error handling across apps.
ideas.currentDocumentation: SDK README mentions 6 error codes; apps/api/CLAUDE.md mentions RFC 7807 but actual API may return more business-specific errors
ideas.proposedContent: Create error code reference: 1) Complete list of error codes with HTTP status codes, 2) Business rule violation errors (BOOKING_CONFLICT, SLOT_UNAVAILABLE, etc.), 3) Recommended UI handling patterns with i18n keys, 4) Rate limiting errors and retry strategies, 5) Validation error format with field-level errors, 6) Authentication/authorization error flow, 7) Tenant isolation errors

ideas.title: Add inline comments to complex booking pricing algorithm
ideas.description: The booking pricing calculation in the SDK (use-booking-quote.ts hook) handles complex scenarios including time-based pricing, participant pricing, seasonal rates, and discount codes, but lacks inline comments explaining the algorithm. The pricing logic spans multiple files without clear documentation of precedence rules.
ideas.rationale: Pricing is business-critical functionality that municipalities rely on for accurate billing. The pricing algorithm handles edge cases like overlapping pricing tiers, participant-based calculations, and discount stacking that are not obvious from code alone. Bugs in pricing could have financial implications for kommune budgets.
ideas.currentDocumentation: Hook functions have basic JSDoc comments but no algorithm explanation; no documentation of pricing tier priority rules
ideas.proposedContent: Add inline comments covering: 1) Pricing tier priority/precedence rules, 2) Time-based calculation formula, 3) Participant pricing logic (per-person vs flat rate), 4) Discount code application order and stacking rules, 5) Minimum/maximum booking constraints, 6) Seasonal rate override rules, 7) Tax calculation (MVA) handling for Norwegian municipalities

ideas.title: Add virtualized list rendering for large data tables
ideas.description: The codebase has multiple list-rendering components (ListingTableView, NotificationCenter, AuditLog, BookingsTab) that render potentially hundreds of items without virtualization. Implement react-window or @tanstack/react-virtual for windowed rendering.
ideas.rationale: Analysis found no virtualization libraries in use. Components like ListingsListView, NotificationCenter, and audit tables can display 100+ items, causing DOM bloat and scroll jank. Each table row creates ~10-20 DOM nodes, meaning 100 rows = 1000-2000 DOM nodes. Virtualization would render only visible rows (~10-15), reducing DOM nodes by 90%+.
ideas.currentMetric: Rendering 100+ items causes noticeable frame drops on mid-range devices
ideas.expectedImprovement: 90%+ reduction in DOM nodes for large lists, 60fps scroll performance, ~200ms faster initial render
ideas.implementation:
1. Install @tanstack/react-virtual
2. Create VirtualizedTable wrapper component in @xala/ds
3. Refactor ListingTableView to use row virtualization
4. Apply to AuditTab, BookingsTab, NotificationCenter
5. Add dynamic row height support for variable content
ideas.tradeoffs: Slightly more complex component code, need to handle dynamic row heights for variable content

ideas.title: Implement route prefetching for predictable navigation patterns
ideas.description: The SDK has React Query integration but minimal prefetching. Analysis found only 3 files with prefetch patterns. Implement smart prefetching for common navigation flows: listing detail from listing list, booking form from listing detail, dashboard data on login.
ideas.rationale: Users follow predictable paths: listing list -> detail -> booking. Currently each route loads data on demand, causing visible loading states. With prefetching, data is already available when user navigates. The SDK already has query key factories in place, making prefetching straightforward to implement.
ideas.currentMetric: Average 400-800ms loading spinner on route transitions
ideas.expectedImprovement: Instant navigation for 70%+ of route transitions, perceived load time < 100ms
ideas.implementation:
1. Add usePrefetch variants to SDK hooks (useRentalObjectPrefetch, useBookingsPrefetch)
2. Prefetch listing detail on row hover in ListingTableView
3. Prefetch booking data when user selects dates
4. Prefetch dashboard KPIs during login callback
5. Use queryClient.prefetchQuery with appropriate staleTime
ideas.tradeoffs: Increased API calls (some wasted if user doesn't navigate), slight memory overhead for cached data

ideas.title: Extract inline arrow functions from event handlers to prevent re-renders
ideas.description: Found 67+ instances of inline arrow functions in onClick handlers across @xala/ds components (ListingTableView, ImageSlider, AvailabilityCalendar, etc.). These create new function references on each render, breaking React.memo optimization and causing unnecessary child re-renders.
ideas.rationale: Inline arrow functions like `onClick={() => handleClick(id)}` create new references every render. When passed to memoized children or used in dependency arrays, they trigger unnecessary re-renders. The BookingSection, ImageSlider, and Calendar components have 3-7 inline handlers each, multiplying the impact.
ideas.currentMetric: Each parent re-render cascades to all children with inline handlers
ideas.expectedImprovement: 50-70% reduction in component re-renders for interactive components, smoother interactions
ideas.implementation:
1. Extract inline handlers to useCallback hooks
2. Pass stable callback references to child components
3. Add React.memo to frequently re-rendered components
4. Use ESLint rule to prevent future inline handlers in @xala/ds
5. Profile before/after with React DevTools Profiler
ideas.tradeoffs: More verbose code with useCallback declarations, need to manage dependency arrays correctly

ideas.title: Add cleanup functions to useEffect hooks with subscriptions/timers
ideas.description: Found 109 usages of addEventListener/setTimeout/setInterval across 76 TSX files. Many useEffect hooks lack proper cleanup functions, risking memory leaks from orphaned event listeners and timers, especially during rapid navigation or component unmounting.
ideas.rationale: Event listeners and timers that aren't cleaned up continue running after component unmount, causing memory leaks and potential errors when they reference stale state. Files like Sidebar.tsx, settings.tsx routes, and various providers have multiple listeners. In a SPA with frequent navigation, this compounds over time.
ideas.currentMetric: Memory grows ~2-5MB per 10 route navigations without page refresh
ideas.expectedImprovement: Stable memory usage during long sessions, prevent 'Can't perform state update on unmounted component' errors
ideas.implementation:
1. Audit all useEffect hooks with addEventListener/setTimeout/setInterval
2. Add cleanup return functions to remove listeners and clear timers
3. Create useEventListener and useTimeout custom hooks in @xala/ds
4. Add ESLint rule to warn about missing cleanup in effects with subscriptions
5. Add memory leak detection to E2E test suite
ideas.tradeoffs: Requires careful review of each useEffect to ensure cleanup logic is correct

ideas.title: Implement request deduplication and batching for dashboard loading
ideas.description: Dashboard pages make multiple parallel API calls (KPIs, stats, activity, pending items, upcoming bookings). While some batching exists with Promise.all, implement systematic request deduplication and GraphQL-style batching to reduce total requests and connection overhead.
ideas.rationale: Dashboard routes fire 5-8 separate useQuery hooks simultaneously. Each creates a separate HTTP request with full overhead (TLS, headers, parsing). The API already has GraphQL via Mercurius. Implement a batch endpoint or leverage DataLoader pattern to combine related queries into single requests.
ideas.currentMetric: Dashboard load triggers 5-8 parallel requests, ~1.2s total waterfall time
ideas.expectedImprovement: Reduce dashboard API calls from 5-8 to 1-2, ~40% faster dashboard load time
ideas.implementation:
1. Create /api/dashboard/batch endpoint accepting array of requested data types
2. Implement DataLoader pattern for automatic request batching
3. Add useDashboardBatch hook combining KPIs, stats, activity into single query
4. Configure React Query to deduplicate identical queries across components
5. Use GraphQL queries for complex dashboard data needs
ideas.tradeoffs: More complex backend logic, need to handle partial failures in batched responses

ideas.title: Extract shared SidebarNavItem component to @xala/ds package
ideas.description: The SidebarNavItem component is nearly identical in both apps/backoffice/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx (408 lines) and apps/minside/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx (498 lines). Both implementations have the same styling patterns, active state handling, badge display logic, and visual structure with only minor differences in props.
ideas.rationale: Code duplication leads to maintenance burden where fixes must be applied in multiple places. As both sidebars share ~80% identical code for the nav item component, extracting to @xala/ds would ensure consistency and reduce total codebase size by ~200 lines.
ideas.currentState: Two separate SidebarNavItem implementations with nearly identical styling, active state logic, and badge rendering. Both use the same design tokens and visual patterns but were developed independently.
ideas.proposedChange: Create packages/ds/src/composed/sidebar-nav.tsx with a configurable SidebarNavItem component that accepts NavItem props, handles active state via react-router-dom integration, and supports badges. Both apps would import and use this shared component with app-specific navigation data.
ideas.bestPractice: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) - extract shared UI components into the design system package

ideas.title: Extract messaging utilities into shared SDK utils
ideas.description: Both apps/backoffice/src/routes/messages.tsx (951 lines) and apps/minside/src/routes/messages.tsx (916 lines) contain duplicated utility functions: formatTimeAgo(), formatMessageDate(), and getTimeAgoKey(). These time formatting utilities are used for conversation timestamps and message grouping.
ideas.rationale: Time formatting utilities are a common need across messaging features. Having two slightly different implementations risks inconsistent behavior and requires maintaining the same logic in multiple places. The SDK already exports formatTime, so these utilities logically belong there.
ideas.currentState: formatTimeAgo(), formatMessageDate(), and related time-relative functions are duplicated. Backoffice version returns Norwegian hardcoded strings ('Nå', 'I dag', 'I går'), while minside version attempts i18n integration but still has hardcoded fallbacks.
ideas.proposedChange: Add formatRelativeTime(), formatMessageGroupDate(), and getRelativeTimeUnit() to packages/client-sdk/src/utils/date-utils.ts. These would return either formatted strings or keys for i18n lookup. Update both message pages to use the shared utilities.
ideas.bestPractice: DRY principle - consolidate date/time utilities in the SDK where they can be tested, documented, and reused
prerequisites: Add relative time and duration formatters to i18n (already planned)

ideas.title: Split ListingAvailabilityCalendar.tsx into mode-specific modules
ideas.description: packages/ds/src/blocks/ListingAvailabilityCalendar.tsx is 1957 lines and handles three distinct calendar modes: TIME_SLOTS (week/day timeline), ALL_DAY (month view with day selection), and MULTI_DAY (date range picker). Each mode has unique rendering logic, state management, and interaction patterns bundled into one massive component.
ideas.rationale: At nearly 2000 lines, this file violates single responsibility principle and is difficult to maintain, test, and review. The three modes are distinct enough that they could be separate components with shared utilities, improving code organization and making each mode easier to understand and modify.
ideas.currentState: Single 1957-line component with mode-specific rendering blocks, shared types, utility functions, and CSS-in-JS styles all in one file. Contains TIME_SLOTS (week view with hourly slots), ALL_DAY (month calendar), and MULTI_DAY (date range) implementations.
ideas.proposedChange: Split into: 1) packages/ds/src/blocks/calendar/types.ts - shared types and constants 2) packages/ds/src/blocks/calendar/TimeSlotsCalendar.tsx - TIME_SLOTS mode 3) packages/ds/src/blocks/calendar/AllDayCalendar.tsx - ALL_DAY mode 4) packages/ds/src/blocks/calendar/MultiDayCalendar.tsx - MULTI_DAY mode 5) packages/ds/src/blocks/calendar/CalendarLegend.tsx - shared legend component 6) packages/ds/src/blocks/ListingAvailabilityCalendar.tsx - thin wrapper that selects the appropriate mode component
ideas.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle - each module should have one reason to change; component files should typically be 300-500 lines
prerequisites: Ensure test coverage exists before refactoring

ideas.title: Split header-parts.tsx into individual component files
ideas.description: packages/ds/src/composed/header-parts.tsx is 1473 lines containing 10+ distinct header subcomponents: HeaderLogo, HeaderSearch, HeaderThemeToggle, HeaderLanguageSelector, HeaderActions, HeaderUserMenu, HeaderNotificationBell, HeaderMobileMenu, HeaderLoginButton, and more. Each component has its own props interface, styles, and logic.
ideas.rationale: The file is essentially a module dump of unrelated components. While they're all 'header parts', they serve different purposes and change for different reasons. This makes the file hard to navigate, increases merge conflict risk, and makes individual components difficult to test in isolation.
ideas.currentState: Single 1473-line file containing HeaderLogo (50 lines), HeaderSearch (200+ lines with animation states), HeaderThemeToggle (100 lines), HeaderLanguageSelector (150 lines), HeaderActions (50 lines), HeaderUserMenu (200+ lines with dropdown), HeaderNotificationBell (100 lines), HeaderMobileMenu (200+ lines), HeaderLoginButton (70 lines), plus helper functions and types.
ideas.proposedChange: Create packages/ds/src/composed/header/ directory with: HeaderLogo.tsx, HeaderSearch.tsx, HeaderThemeToggle.tsx, HeaderLanguageSelector.tsx, HeaderActions.tsx, HeaderUserMenu.tsx, HeaderNotificationBell.tsx, HeaderMobileMenu.tsx, HeaderLoginButton.tsx, types.ts (shared types), and index.ts (barrel export). Keep backward-compatible re-exports from header-parts.tsx.
ideas.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle and file organization - each component in its own file makes the codebase easier to navigate and reduces cognitive load

ideas.title: Convert booking-engine/styles.ts CSS-in-JS to CSS modules
ideas.description: packages/ds/src/blocks/booking-engine/styles.ts is a 1500-line file containing CSS template strings for the UnifiedBookingEngine component. This CSS-in-JS approach creates a massive string that gets injected at runtime, hurts performance, and makes styles difficult to maintain, lint, and debug.
ideas.rationale: CSS-in-JS template strings at this scale have several drawbacks: no syntax highlighting or linting in the string, runtime style injection overhead, difficult to identify unused styles, and no CSS module scoping. Converting to CSS modules would improve developer experience, enable IDE support, and potentially reduce bundle size through CSS minification.
ideas.currentState: 1500 lines of CSS in a template literal string exported as unifiedBookingEngineStyles. Contains ~50 CSS classes for header, stepper, calendar, pricing, confirmation, and other booking engine sections. The style tag is injected into the component on render.
ideas.proposedChange: Convert to packages/ds/src/blocks/booking-engine/styles.module.css (or .css if not using modules). Update the component to import and use CSS class names. This enables CSS tooling, better tree-shaking, and proper CSS minification. As an alternative, consider converting to Tailwind utility classes if the project moves in that direction.
ideas.bestPractice: Prefer CSS files over CSS-in-JS for large style blocks - enables better tooling, IDE support, and optimization
prerequisites: Verify CSS module support in build configuration
